subject: Trading
title: Kelly Criterion
description: A short lesson to help you apply Kelly Criterion.

hook.text: A formula from 1956 tells you the mathematically optimal bet size. Traders use it, but with a crucial caveat.

buildup.text: The Kelly Criterion: f = (bp − q) / b, where b is payoff odds, p is win probability, and q is loss probability.

discovery.text: Kelly maximizes long-term growth rate. A 60% win rate with 1:1 payoff suggests risking 20% of capital.

twist.text: Full Kelly is extremely aggressive. Most practitioners use 'half Kelly' or less to reduce volatility and drawdowns.

climax.text: Kelly proves that over-betting is as harmful as under-betting. There's a mathematical sweet spot for position size.

punchline.text: Optimal size exists. Over-betting destroys wealth.

quiz.question: Why do most traders use half Kelly instead of full Kelly?
options: Full Kelly is too aggressive—half Kelly reduces volatility and drawdowns
